newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FAI says looking for bank partnerships.
newsitem.headline: FAI says looking for bank partnerships.

text.p: FAI Insurances Ltd chief executive Rodney Adler said on Wednesday the group was looking for a "strategic partnership" with an Australian bank, aimed at expanding its national home loan business.
"I would love to have a strategic partnership with an Australian bank," Adler told reporters after an Australia-Israel Chamber of Commerce meeting.
Adler said FAI would prefer a partnership arrangement rather than applying for a bank licence in its own right.
"I can't see any advantage in being a bank ourselves today," he said.
"We have all the attributes and characteristics of being a bank without becoming a bank," he said.
Adler said FAI would also enter a strategic partnership with a foreign bank "if it is helpful for us to grow in some parts of Asia."
He said FAI was looking to grow its Asian premium income which currently stood at about seven percent of total business.
"We'd like to see that go to about 15 to 20 percent over the next five or six years," he said.
He said there was no money to be made in the Australian home loan mortgage market for single bank and non-bank providers.
"You cannot start in that (mortgage provider) market now - there's no money in it," Adler said.
FAI currently was writing about A$40 million a month in its home loan division and was already the second biggest in the market after Aussie Home Loans Ltd, he said.
Earlier Adler said FAI was expecting to make a statement before its June financial year-end on new insurance products to be conducted on the Internet.
"We hope to be one of the first to have insurance on the Internet, primarily with car, home and commercial insurance products payable by credit card," Adler said in his speech.
FAI had outsourced Internet computer technology to produce its products to the United States-based PMS group, Adler said.
"We hope to have eventually a virtual insurance office on the Internet - the minute someone debugs it (the Internet) we want to be on top of it," Adler said.
